predecessors.note: The Cumania infobox: 'Preceded by Kimek-Kipchak confederation and Khazaria'. This is lineage, not a handover of land: the Kimek-Kipchak dossier (ia-01-e) lists only mongol-empire as successor and continues itself in 1055 as 'the confederation continues here under its Kipchak-Cuman names' (its rename), so the two dossiers carry one people on either side of a seam. The land listed is the steppe the Cumans came to hold, which the Cumans page has the Cumans take as they press the Oghuz west and, through them, the Pechenegs west of the Dnieper (no years), not land the Kimek row ever held. Open for the orchestrator with ia-01-e: one dossier listing both Cliopatria Names, or a 1055 split in the Kimek dossier naming this one. The page gives no handover from Khazaria, which ended long before.

land.text: the Cuman steppe with the Bugeac, outside the Kimek-Kipchak row's 1072 shape (28-49 E), which the Cumans entered 'around 1068-1078'

successors.note: 'The final blow came in 1241, when Cuman control over the Pontic steppes ended', and the remaining Cumans became subjects 'as part of what was to be known as the Golden Horde (Kipchak Khanate)' (the page): the Pontic steppe passes to the Jochid ulus, the later Golden Horde, which is a constituent of the Mongol Empire (hierarchy.csv); the ulus-of-jochi dossier carries the matching gain of 1241 over the Pontic Steppe region. Cliopatria's Golden Horde row starts only in 1294. (fx-35, 1 Nov 2026: was mongol-empire, which left ulus-of-jochi unable to gain the land.) The Cuman remnant under Köten (Kotyan) fled to Hungary, the Danube and Byzantine service (not territory of this state).

keyframe_review.note: 1056-1065, 315 km2 (one H3 cell at 26.2 E, 48.6 N, Podolia near Kamianets-Podilskyi and Khotyn, shapes.csv 315 km2): no page puts the Cumans there. The Cumans page has them first meet the Rus' in 1055 at the Pereyaslavl frontier ('The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055, when they advanced towards the Rus' Pereyaslavl principality'), ravage Pereyaslavl in 1061 and win the Alta River in 1068, and enter the Bugeac only 'around 1068-1078'. The Cumania page gives no area (infobox: none), so no infobox comparison; the 11th-12th century realm 'dominated lands from present-day Kazakhstan and southern Russia, through Ukraine, to southern Moldavia and eastern Wallachia'. Replaced by the Pontic-Caspian steppe outside the Kimek row (28-49 E: the Dnieper-Danube steppe and the lower Don, Kuban and Kalmyk steppe; confidence 1 on the extent: neither page draws a boundary). Cliopatria's Halych-Volhynia occupation row holds 831 cells of the same steppe (29-39 E) in 1056-1240.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1055-1071: the Pontic-Caspian steppe outside the Kimek-Kipchak row's 1056 shape, from the Rus' frontier at Pereyaslavl (first contact 1055) to the Black Sea and out to the lower Don, Kuban and Kalmyk steppe (cells from 28 to 49 E; a first version said the steppe stopped at 38 E, but 855 of its 1,815 cells lie east of 38.5 E, reviewer ia-01-g). Neither page gives a boundary; the Pontic Steppe region of the gazetteer ('between the Dnieper, Volga, Ural and Irtysh' on the Cumania page) minus the Kimek row's 1056 shape is the reading (confidence 1 for the extent). The Bugeac (52 cells) is left out until 1078, when the ledger has the Cumans enter it. The Cumania page's 'dominated lands from present-day Kazakhstan and southern Russia, through Ukraine, to southern Moldavia and eastern Wallachia' reaches further east than this dossier draws; that land is the Kimek-Kipchak dossier's.

The Bugeac lies inside the gazetteer's Pontic Steppe region, which is why the earlier keyframes leave it out. Wallachia and Moldavia appear on the page without dates, and the Cuman raids and conquests across the Danube (Paristrion in 1094-1095) are raids that the page does not show as held; not drawn.

ledger.note: 1055: the Cumans appear on the Pontic steppe at the Rus' frontier. 'The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055, when they advanced towards the Rus' Pereyaslavl principality'; Prince Vsevolod reached an agreement with them and battle was avoided. The Cumania infobox dates the confederation to the '10th century'; 1055 is the first date for its western steppe. The land's previous holders, from the Cumans page: the Cumans' entry into the area 'pressed the Oghuz Turks to shift west', 'which in turn caused the Pechenegs to move to the west of the Dnieper River' (no years), and 'Cuman and Rus' attacks contributed to the departure of the Oghuz from the steppes north of the Black Sea'. The steppe was therefore the Oghuz and Pecheneg land, not the Kimek row's; the counterpart stays the Kimek-Kipchak dossier only because the Cumania infobox names it as predecessor (a lineage, see identity), and the Cumans page gives no handover from it (reviewer ia-01-g).

region.text: the 447 cells (about 113,000 km2, the Volga steppe) of this steppe that Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak row takes in 1072

ledger.note: 1072: Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape grows into 447 cells of this dossier's steppe (the Kimek dossier's 1072 gain of 'the southern Urals, Bashkortostan and the eastern and middle Volga') and keeps them to 1235. Neither the Cumans nor the Cumania page dates or draws it. The two dossiers cover one people (Cumania infobox: preceded by the Kimek-Kipchak confederation), so this loss only stops the same cells from being claimed twice (reviewer ia-01-g); the Kimek dossier's gain should name this dossier instead of 'nobody' (ia-01-e). Confidence 1.

1078: the Cumans hold the Bugeac. 'The Cumans first entered the Bugeac (Bessarabia) at some point around 1068-1078.' The page gives a span, not a year, and does not say who held the land before. The counterpart is a reading: the page has the Cuman entry press the Oghuz Turks west and 'in turn' move the Pechenegs 'to the west of the Dnieper River' (no years), and the Bugeac lies west of the Dnieper, so the Pechenegs are named (confidence 2; a Pecheneg dossier is still needed). The page dates none of these moves.

ledger.note: 1241: the Cuman confederation ends. Cumania infobox 'Disestablished: 1241'; the remaining tribes 'being dispersed, either becoming subjects and mixing with their Mongol conquerors' or fleeing to Hungary and the Danube. The steppe passes to the Jochid ulus, the Golden Horde to be: the remaining Cumans stayed 'as part of what was to be known as the Golden Horde (Kipchak Khanate) and Nogai Horde' (fx-35: counterpart was mongol-empire; the 1238 attack and the 1241 end of the contest stay with the Mongol Empire, since the page names only 'the Mongols' as attackers).

wars.name: Cuman wars with the Rus' princes
wars.outcome: In 1061 the Cumans under Sokal 'invaded and devastated the Pereyaslavl principality', which 'began a war that would go on for 175 years'; no frontier changed hands on the pages opened.
wars.note: Main dated episodes: 1068 the Alta River, 1093 the defeat of Monomakh, 1096-1107 Boniak's raids on Kiev, 1107 his defeat near Lubny. The Rus' princes also used Cuman allies (1097-1099 against Hungary at Przemysl, 1104 with Volodar).

wars.name: Battle of the Alta River
wars.outcome: 'In 1068 at the Battle of the Alta River, the Cumans defeated the armies of the three sons of Yaroslav the Wise' (Iziaslav of Kiev, Sviatoslav of Chernigov, Vsevolod of Pereyaslavl).

wars.name: Cuman raids on Byzantium and Hungary
wars.outcome: Joint raid with the Pechenegs on Adrianople in 1078; Balkan raids from 1086; defeat by Ladislaus I of Hungary in 1089; the Pechenegs broken at Levounion in 1091 by Byzantines and Cumans; Paristrion 'conquered' in 1094-1095; Boniak crushes the Hungarian army in 1099. No frontier is given.

wars.note: Kalka (1223) was an earlier Mongol defeat of the Cumans and their Rus' allies; the Cumania infobox ends the confederation in 1241.

certainty.note: A nomadic steppe confederation: neither page draws a frontier, and the extent of the steppe is the gazetteer's Pontic Steppe region minus the Kimek-Kipchak row (28-49 E).

notes:
Cliopatria row: one 315 km2 shape (a single cell in Podolia) for 1056-1065; wrong, replaced by four keyframes of the Pontic-Caspian steppe outside the Kimek-Kipchak row (1055-1071, 1072-1077, 1078-1241, plus the verdict on the Cliopatria shape). The row ends in 1065 but the pages keep the confederation to 1241, so the dossier runs 1055-1241, with the 1055 start taken from the page's first contact (the infobox says '10th century').
Relation to the Kimek-Kipchak dossier (ia-01 group): that dossier runs the same Kipchak-Cuman people from 880 to 1241 on the steppe of its own Cliopatria shapes and renames itself in 1055, without naming this dossier as successor; this dossier is the steppe outside that row's 1056 shape (28-49 E: the Dnieper-Danube steppe and the lower Don, Kuban and Kalmyk steppe; a first version said the steppe stopped at 38 E, which was wrong for 855 of its 1,815 cells). From 1072 the Kimek row grows into 447 cells of that steppe, so this dossier loses them in 1072 (ledger, confidence 1); the Kimek dossier's 1072 gain should name this dossier. Open for the orchestrator with ia-01-e: one dossier for the confederation listing both Cliopatria Names, or a 1055 split in the Kimek dossier naming cuman-kipchak-confederation. Cliopatria's Halych-Volhynia occupation row (eu-16) draws about 830-880 cells of the same steppe as Galician-Volhynian land in 1056-1240; the compile stage must decide which wins. The Pontic Steppe region of the gazetteer is 720,000 km2; minus the Kimek row's 1056 shape it is 459,000 km2 (1,815 cells), and without the 447 cells and the Bugeac 1,316 cells (333,000 km2) from 1072.
Capital: dropped in the review fix. The infobox gives 'Capital: Sarai' with no years; Sarai (45.35 E, 48.68 N) is the Golden Horde's seat, later than this confederation, and lies outside every shape of this dossier. The confederation was nomadic and the pages give no seat, so the list is empty.
Pages: Cumans (four queries) and Cumania (one query), the budget of 1-2. Neither gives an area, a frontier, an 11th-century khan other than Sokal (1061), or a Cuman seat; the extent of the steppe is therefore confidence 1. Missing: Pechenegs and Torks as predecessors or neighbours (no dossier; the Bugeac gain names pechenegs as counterpart); the Cuman remnant in Hungary (Cumania as a Hungarian county after 1241) and the Danube (Wallachia, Moldavia); Kotyan's 1239-1241 exodus; Kalka 1223 (a note in the Mongol war only); Byzantine Paristrion, which the page calls conquered in 1094-1095 without saying it was held.
